A hands-on short course for researchers, public health professionals and
students who want to strengthen both the theory and the practice of
epidemiology. Lectures alternate with hands-on training. You will leave able to
choose a study design, compute and interpret the measures that design produces,
tell a real effect from a biased one, and do all of it in R in a way someone
else can rerun.

## Before you arrive
There are 5 things to do before Monday 21 September. They take about 4 hours in
total. Spread them over several evenings. Installing the software is the only
one we cannot fix for you on the day.

→ [**Start here: the 5 steps**](prelude/index.qmd)

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The programme is being finalised and will be circulated separately.
:::

## What you will be able to do

::: {.card-grid}

::: {.card-tile}
### Measure disease
Turn counts into prevalence, risk, rate and person-time, and say out loud
which one a given question needs.
:::

::: {.card-tile}
### Measure association
Build a 2×2 table and read a risk ratio, an odds ratio, a risk difference and
a number needed to treat off it without looking anything up.
:::

::: {.card-tile}
### Choose a design
Match a research question to a cohort, case-control, cross-sectional or trial
design, and know what each one can and cannot tell you.
:::

::: {.card-tile}
### Spot bias
Name the bias you are looking at: selection, information, confounding. Tell
confounding from interaction, and handle each correctly.
:::

::: {.card-tile}
### Analyse in R
Import, clean, summarise and plot epidemiological data with the tidyverse,
instead of clicking through a menu you cannot document.
:::

::: {.card-tile}
### Work reproducibly
Organise an analysis so a colleague, a reviewer, or you in six months can
rerun every number in your paper from the raw data.
:::

:::

## Who this is for

Researchers, public health professionals, programme managers and students. No
prior programming is assumed. If you have used SPSS, Excel or Stata you already
understand most of the statistical ideas; this course changes the tools and
sharpens the reasoning.

You need a laptop you can install software on, and about 4 hours before the
course to work through the [prelude](prelude/index.qmd).
